chunks: From him, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon them both), that Ali (peace be upon him) said:
The imprisonment of the Imam after the fixed punishment (hudud) is injustice.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on imprisoning the Imam after he has received his hudud punishment?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this narration by Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq clarifies the distinction between the execution of a fixed penalty (hadd) and administrative detention, asserting that prolonged imprisonment without new legal grounds constitutes oppression (zulm). This principle underscores the Imam's role as the ultimate arbiter of justice, ensuring that punitive measures do not exceed their prescribed limits, a concept deeply rooted in the legal theories of Shaykh al-Tusi in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*.
